lean.statement:
theorem anonymous_target {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X]
    (μ : Measure X) [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (κ : Kernel X X) [IsMarkovKernel κ] (hκ : κ.Invariant μ) :
    ∃ A : Lp ℝ 2 μ →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 μ, ‖A‖ ≤ 1 ∧
      (∀ f : X → ℝ, ∀ hf : MemLp f 2 μ,
        (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Integrable f (κ x)) ∧
        (A (hf.toLp f) : X → ℝ) =ᵐ[μ] fun x => ∫ z, f z ∂κ x) ∧
      (∀ f : Lp ℝ 2 μ, (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ f x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ A f x) ∧
      A (Lp.const 2 μ (1 : ℝ)) = Lp.const 2 μ (1 : ℝ) ∧
      (∀ f : Lp ℝ 2 μ, (∫ x, A f x ∂μ) = ∫ x, f x ∂μ) ∧
      (κ.IsReversible μ → IsSelfAdjoint A)
approved_definition_context: Lp R 2 mu is the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real functions modulo mu-almost-everywhere equality. MemLp f 2 mu includes AE strong measurability and a finite L2 norm. hf.toLp f is its quotient class. The coerced function of any Lp element is a chosen representative; equalities of such functions are stated almost everywhere.

IsFiniteMeasure allows zero or any finite nonnegative mass, not just probability. Kernel X X is a measurable family of measures, and IsMarkovKernel requires a probability measure at every input. Kernel.Invariant k mu means mu.bind k=mu.

Kernel.IsReversible k mu means that for every pair of measurable sets A,B, the nonnegative extended-real integral of k(x,B) over A with mu equals the integral of k(x,A) over B. This is a measurable-rectangle condition, not an assertion only about singleton probabilities.

A continuous real-linear map has its operator norm. Lp.const 2 mu 1 is the quotient class of the constant-one function. The real Bochner integral is totalized, so genuine integrability is a separate mathematical assertion. IsSelfAdjoint A means its Hilbert adjoint equals A. All AE quantifiers have exactly the displayed measure and parameter scope.
